# rust-webx-outbox-ef

Transactional outbox for `rust-webx` events, over `rust-ef`.

The application writes the outbox row **inside the same transaction as the
business data**; a `PeriodicBackgroundService` later claims due rows, dispatches
each event through the process's `#[handler] IEventHandler<T>` registrations,
and marks it delivered or retries with exponential backoff (dead-lettering after
`MaxAttempts`).

```rust
use webx_outbox_ef::{OutboxDbContextExt, OutboxOptions, register_outbox_model};

// 1. Register the table in the application's DbContext model (migrations
//    generated by the official rust-ef tooling).
register_outbox_model(&mut ctx);

// 2. Enqueue inside the business transaction.
ctx.use_transaction(|ctx| async move {
    ctx.add(Order { /* ... */ });
    ctx.enqueue_outbox(&OrderPlaced { order_id })?;
    ctx.save_changes().await
}).await?;

// 3. Start the dispatcher.
Host::builder()
    .add_outbox_ef(OutboxOptions::default())
    .build();
```

Delivery is **at-least-once**: a crash between a successful dispatch and the
`delivered_at` update re-delivers the event, so handlers must be idempotent.
Only one instance claims a row at a time (lease + compare-and-set), so a crashed
worker's rows are reclaimed after `LeaseSeconds`.
